"BUILD A BETTER FUTURE" — Sir George Williams College building-fund prospectus, 1952
and a map of the Y's Greater Montreal properties

Internet Archive identifier: sgw-build-a-better-future
Creator: Sir George Williams College | date 1952 | one _djvu.txt, 37,916 chars
Archive description: "Prospectus for a fundraising campaign for the Sir George
Williams College Building Fund."
Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).
Not previously in sources.json.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT THE DOCUMENT IS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A donor prospectus for a new College building. Its argument: the Evening
Division is "bursting at the seams," several hundred students were turned away
last year, the Drummond-Stanley Building "originally provided accommodation for
only 2,000," four rented annexes "are not designed for educational work;
conditions are crowded and makeshift," and the target is to accommodate 6,000
in the Evening Division. "The Survey and Policy Committee of the YMCA has
recommended that this need be met by constructing a new classroom and
administration building" — a four-storey structure beside the Drummond-Stanley
Building, in which the College would retain 23,000 square feet on two floors.
It names Principal Norris, Dean Henry F. Hall and Bursar Henry G. Worrell
reviewing the blueprints.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHERE THE CAMPS APPEAR, AND WHAT KIND OF EVIDENCE THAT IS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

READ THIS BEFORE USING THE PASSAGE. The camp names do NOT occur in a sentence.
They are labels on a MAP, captioned "HERE IS YOUR Y.M.C.A. OF GREATER MONTREAL",
and what the OCR returns is the scattered label text in reading order with the
cartography lost:

  "CAMP OTOREKE   CAMP KANAWANA   CAMP PERROT   GOUIN BLVD   CHRISTIEVILLE SKI
  LODGE   …TO … LAURENTIANS …  ST. MICHEL RD.   INTERNATIONAL   COTE DE LIESSE
  CENTRAL Y.M.C.A.   ROSEMOUNT   NEW SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE   NOTRE DAME DE
  GRACE   …SHERBROOKE…   WESTMOUNT   …CITY HALL…   BRANCH
  HERE IS YOUR Y.M.C.A. OF GREATER MONTREAL"

Legend fragments follow: "Building Fund", "Other Projects", "Y.M.C.A. Branches".

SO WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE TAKEN FROM IT. What can: that in 1952 a Sir George
Williams College fundraising prospectus put THE THREE CAMPS AND THE
CHRISTIEVILLE SKI LODGE on a single map of the Association's Greater Montreal
holdings, alongside the branches and the proposed new College building, under
the heading "your Y.M.C.A." What cannot: any spatial relationship, any distance,
any symbol-to-legend assignment, or which items were marked "Building Fund"
against "Other Projects". Those are properties of a graphic and the OCR of a
graphic does not preserve them. THE PAGE IMAGE WOULD SETTLE THEM AND HAS NOT
BEEN LOOKED AT.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TWO THINGS WORTH HAVING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. CHRISTIEVILLE SKI LODGE IS ON A DONOR MAP IN 1952. wiki/site/camp-otoreke.md
   records, from Concordia's finding aid, a "Purchase by YMCA of Christieville
   property. - 1948-1951", a "Friendly Home-Christieville rental" (1948), the
   "Christieville site" (1949) and "Christieville ski lodge correspondence"
   (1959) — a property the wiki says "the Y appears to have acquired… and run
   for at least a decade." This is the middle of that decade and it is not a
   file title: the lodge was established enough by 1952 to be worth showing
   donors by name.

2. THE CAMPS ARE INSIDE THE COLLEGE'S OWN FUNDRAISING FAMILY. This is a SIR
   GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE prospectus, and the map it prints is of the YMCA's
   properties with the College as one item among them. It is the same identity
   that runs through everything found today — the college on the second and
   third floors of the Drummond Street Y building, the Training Fellowship men
   staffing the camps, Camp Otoreke in the college calendar — seen here from the
   fundraising side, where a donor is asked to think of the camps and the
   college as one institution's estate.

NULL RESULTS. Each of Kanawana, Otoreke, Perrot, Christieville and Gouin occurs
EXACTLY ONCE in the whole 37,916-character document, all of them in this map.
There is no prose about any camp anywhere in the prospectus.
